newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico rejects linking peso to dollar - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico rejects linking peso to dollar - paper.

text.p: Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said in an interview published on Tuesday that he rejected a proposal to link the peso to the dollar.

Refering to a suggestion from U.S. economist Rudiger Dornbusch, Ortiz told the daily El Financiero that under current circumstances, the proposal to link the peso to the dollar cannot be seriously considered.

Ortiz said the proposal had advantages and disadvantages. "It could well give more confidence to investors with respect to the exchange rate, (but) in the event of an external shock, the unfavorable impact would be greater," Ortiz said.
Ortiz added that the government's current floating foreign regime -- under which the goverment intervenes sporadically to quell market volatility -- had worked well in the last few years.
But he added as inflation pressures lessened, the floating foreign regime would become less important.
Ortiz said for the moment it was better for the country to have "maximum flexibility in its foreign exchange regime".
Nonetheless, Ortiz added it was necessary to continuing debating the country's foreign exchange policies and other economic topics of national interest.
